question: Must an integrated complex organ evolve as an integrated unit?
frozen_split_rule: TRAIN/VALIDATION individual IDs are frozen before phenotype-linked genomic discovery and cannot be changed after candidate blocks are seen.

F.label: fixed_evolutionary_integration
F.constraint: multiple blocks allowed but focal trait effects pass through one shared latent genomic score or equivalent rank-1 block-by-trait effect structure

R.label: reconfigurable_integration
R.constraint: component-specific genomic scores allowed under the same training data and complexity budget; genomic effect rank may exceed one; residual phenotypic covariance allowed

primary_estimand.test: paired one-sided sign-flip test over validation individuals
r_support: joint advantage not driven solely by one primary component

secondary_estimand.rule: component-associated local genomic-state concordance is compared with matched genomic blocks; discordance alone is insufficient unless those states independently predict component phenotypes

kill_shot_estimand.rule: prospective mosaic status is registered before validation phenotype labels are opened; both primary components must be correctly predicted under the frozen componentwise model; reference and taxonomic QC must pass

decisions.FIG3_R_STRONG: E1 supports R; both primary components have stable genomic contribution; genomic states are separable; at least 3 prospective validation mosaics correctly predicted; reference-stable.
decisions.FIG3_R_PARTIAL: R improves prediction but one component, validation route or mosaic count is insufficient for the full kill shot.
decisions.FIG3_F_SUPPORTIVE: Shared-state F predicts as well or better and component-specific states collapse onto the same inherited state.
decisions.NOT_IDENTIFIABLE: Signal, reference stability, validation sample size or biological confounding prevents discrimination.
